p: The Royal Greenwich Observatory moved to Herstmonceux after the Second World War, seeking clearer skies away from London's pollution and light. It stayed until 1990, when it moved to Cambridge, and today the old domes are a reminder of a fascinating chapter in British astronomy.

Herstmonceux Castle, a striking 15th-century moated castle built from brick, is now owned by Queen's University in Canada and used as a study centre. Its gardens and grounds are open to visitors at certain times of year.

Nearby, Pevensey Castle has Roman walls and a medieval castle all in one, and it was here, in 1066, that William the Conqueror landed before the Battle of Hastings. Battle Abbey, built on the site of the famous battle, is a short drive away, as is the fairytale moated Bodiam Castle.
For seaside fun, Eastbourne has a Victorian pier and a long promenade, and Beachy Head and the Seven Sisters cliffs offer some of the most spectacular coastal walks in the country.
At the science centre, pack a picnic, wear comfy shoes and allow at least half a day.

There's something special about standing among those old domes, knowing that some of the country's top astronomers once spent long nights here charting the heavens. It's a lovely way to get kids thinking about space and science as real jobs done by real people. Bring a flask and enjoy the big Sussex skies.
